statement: A session claiming or working a quest is shown every declared-scope path it shares with any other live session before its first attempt seals, from the shared registry rather than local solve state, and the warning names the peer worktree and the exact overlapping paths.

constraints.statement: If this Quest changes source code, spawn a subagent verifier before audit and git handoff, then record a Solver finding with evidence subagent:<id>.

Overlap detection reads other sessions' declared scopes from the shared registry; a peer's in-flight scope lives in its own worktree's solve state and is invisible to local scans, so local-only detection is a refuted design.
Scope overlap warns with the peer worktree and exact shared paths; it never blocks an attempt — overlapping work is sometimes intended, and the lease (not the advisory) is the exclusivity mechanism.
The advisory is only as good as declared scopes; the claim flow makes declaring scope cheap (claim --scope), and an empty declaration produces no false confidence output.
